payload.scope: People made the thyroid cartilage construct to identify the paired laryngeal cartilage forming the anterior framework of the larynx and housing the vocal folds, so that clinicians can locate it for surgical landmarks, airway access, and voice disorder treatment.

definition.body: The thyroid cartilage is the human-authored anatomical construct identifying the paired laminae that fuse anteriorly to form the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple) and provide the anterior and lateral framework of the larynx, anchoring the vocal folds and intrinsic muscles. Parameters: (1) the laminae — two quadrilateral plates that meet at the anterior median angle; (2) the laryngeal prominence — the anterior ridge formed by the superior and inferior thyroid crests, palpable as the Adam's apple; (3) the superior and inferior horns — posterior extensions of each lamina providing attachment points for ligaments and membranes; (4) the external surface — attachments for the sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, and inferior constrictor muscles; (5) the internal surface — attachments for the thyrohyoid membrane and the vocal ligament. It persists as a standard anatomical landmark in human anatomy texts, laryngology, and airway management, providing the structural referent for laryngeal framework surgery, tracheostomy, and laryngoplasty procedures. e.g.: the thyroid cartilage anatomy shown in Gray's Anatomy, 51st edition; the laryngeal prominence palpated during thyroid examination per Bates' Guide to Physical Examination; open laryngectomy with thyroid cartilage resection for advanced glottic cancer per the VA Laryngeal Cancer Study | not: the cricoid cartilage (complete ring-shaped cartilage below the thyroid); the thyroid gland (endocrine organ, distinct from laryngeal cartilage) [formal: cartilago thyroidea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

definition.body: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the branch of the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) that ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove to innervate all intrinsic laryngeal muscles and provide sensory input to the laryngeal mucosa below the vocal folds. Parameters: (1) the recurrent course — the right nerve hooks under the right subclavian artery and ascends vertically; the left nerve loops under the aortic arch lateral to the ligamentum arteriosum before ascending — a difference arising from embryological migration of the arch arteries; (2) the sensory distribution — supplies mucosa of the larynx inferior to the vocal folds, including the piriform fossa; (3) the motor distribution — innervates the posterior cricoarytenoid (abductor), lateral cricoarytenoid (adductor), thyroarytenoid (relaxer), vocalis (fine-tuner), and interarytenoid (adductor) muscles; (4) the anatomical course — ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove between the trachea and esophagus, entering the larynx posterior to the inferior constrictor. definition.body: The vocal ligament is the human-authored anatomical construct identifying the paired elastic fibrous band that extends from the vocal process of the arytenoid cartilage anteriorly to the angle of the thyroid cartilage, forming the structural core of the vocal fold. Parameters: (1) the course — runs from the anterior vocal process to the thyroid angle at the midline; (2) the composition — dense connective tissue rich in elastic fibers; (3) the mechanical role — provides tensile strength to the vocal fold; (4) the surgical landmark — the plane where microlaryngeal instruments approach for excision or grafting. Parameters: (1) the location — spans the gap between the cricoid arch anteriorly and the thyroid cartilage inferior horn, bounded medially by the cricothyroid ligament (median thyrohyoid membrane); (2) the composition — dense irregular connective tissue with elastic fibers, thicker and more compliant than the median cricothyroid ligament; (3) the vascular supply — the anterior and posterior superior laryngeal arteries from the superior thyroid artery; (4) the clinical landmark — the most superficial structure between the airway and the skin surface, targeted in emergency cricothyroidotomy; (5) the surgical access plane — the midline puncture or incision site for emergency surgical airway when endotracheal intubation is impossible. definition.body: The piriform fossa is the human-authored anatomical construct identifying the paired mucosal depressions flanking the laryngeal inlet, extending from the aryepiglottic folds superiorly to the postcricoid region inferiorly and bounded laterally by the thyroid cartilage. Parameters: (1) the boundaries — medial wall formed by the aryepiglottic fold and lateral cricoarytenoid muscle; lateral wall by the thyroid cartilage inner surface; (2) the mucosal lining — stratified squamous epithelium continuous with pharyngeal and esophageal mucosa; (3) the contents — the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the mucosa; (4) the clinical significance — common site for foreign body impaction and target for blind nasal intubation; (5) the surgical relevance — traversed during endoscopic approaches and important for metastatic spread from hypopharyngeal carcinoma. It persists as a standard anatomical landmark in otolaryngology and gastroenterology. e.g.: piriform fossa foreign body impaction in Cummings Otolaryngology 6th edition; piriform fossa evaluation during swallowing videofluoroscopy; piriform fossa innervation by the internal laryngeal nerve in anesthesia texts [not: the piriform sinus; the epiglottis [formal: sinus piriformis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

definition.body: The laryngopharynx is the human-authored anatomical construct identifying the inferior portion of the pharynx extending from the epiglottis superiorly to the esophagus inferiorly, and from the aryepiglottic folds laterally. Parameters: (1) the boundaries — extends from the upper border of the epiglottis to the lower border of the cricoid cartilage at C6 level; (2) the subdivisions — the piriform fossae laterally and the postcricoid region anteriorly; (3) the mucosal lining — stratified squamous epithelium continuous with the esophagus; (4) the functional role — shared conduit for respiratory and digestive tracts with the laryngeal inlet opening anteriorly; (5) the clinical significance — site of hypopharyngeal carcinoma and key region in swallow mechanics. It persists as a standard anatomical landmark in otolaryngology and gastroenterology. e.g.: laryngopharynx anatomy in Cummings Otolaryngology 6th edition; postcricoid region in videofluoroscopic swallow study; hypopharyngeal carcinoma in AJCC 8th edition [not: the oropharynx; the esophagus [formal: pharynx laryngea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
